newsitem.title: UK: U.S. environmentalists launch new attack on Shell.
newsitem.headline: U.S. environmentalists launch new attack on Shell.

text.p: Two U.S.-based activist groups added their weight to growing criticsm of Royal Dutch/Shell Group's environmental and human rights policies on Tuesday .
A day before the oil giant's annual shareholder meetings, the groups accused Shell of not improving its act despite despite recent company environmental initiatives.
"There is a great gulf between Shell's rhetoric and day-to-day practice in the countries the company is operating in," said Shannon Wright, campaign director of Rainforest Action Network.
At a news conference here, the Californian-based group presented a highly critical report of Shell's operations in Peru and Nigeria.
In the document, produced jointly with Project Underground, Shell is accused of spilling oil in Peruvian rivers, ignoring the views of local peoples and colluding with the Nigerian army.
The groups say drinking water in the Niger Delta, where Shell is active, is polluted by oil. Water contamination there is up to 680 times higher than allowed in Europe, the groups claim.
In addition, they allege that Shell is set to drill inside a protected reserve for two nomadic peoples in Peru.
"In less than a year of operations (in Peru), Shell has already broken key promises for respect of indigenous rights and community consultation," Wright said.
Shell dismissed the criticism. "It is inaccurate and misleading ....it recycles old and discredited myths and tries to create an artificial linkage between Nigeria and Peru," a spokesman said.
The accusations come as shareholders in London and The Hague are set to vote on Wednesday on a resolution calling for an independent environmental audit of Shell's activities.
Shell has urged shareholders to reject the resolution and tried to diffuse criticism by publishing its own first worldwide environment report last week.

But rebel shareholders, led by Pensions & Investment Research Consultants (PIRC), call for tougher measures, although realising that the resolution for an external audit stands little chance of being accepted.
"But it shows there is clearly a wind of change," said Richard Boele, human rights campaigner of cosmetics retailer Body Shop.
Body Shop is one of about two dozen groups such as Friends of the Earth expressing their concern over Shell's environmental and human rights record in a public letter.
The groups will hand out the letter to investors at Wednesday's shareholder meetings.
